📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The uproar over the alleged use of generative AI imagery in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” has taken a familiar path. Early responses to the Netflix film penned by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher have pointed out egregious examples of generative video artifacts sticking out in key flashback moments in the film — including one shot from the trailer where it certainly looks like a video AI program rendered a wagon the wrong way around.

It has been revealed that the criticism is of the use of generative AI in principle as a fundamental betrayal of the creative process — but it’s also of Fincher, as a director who, historically, has been meticulous with the level of detail and intention in every single shot of his films. In the early responses to Fincher’s latest, there’s been a lot of surprise and disappointment about this particular filmmaker being caught up in an AI controversy. Related Stories Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch.

It has been revealed that at first blush, his approach seems at odds with using generative AI video, which relies on regurgitated (and, it bears repeating every time, stolen) data. But Fincher has defended his use of AI to the LA Times as a way to continue to innovate on an art form that is, after all, just over a hundred years old.

That defense really shouldn’t be surprising, given Fincher’s history with AI specifically. Although he’s been critical of generative tools in the past, Fincher admitted to using them (never publicly disclosing which) in the 4K remaster of “Se7en,” which the director described as a process of needing to remake the negative in order to battle the ravages of time (and the thousands of tiny scratches that would show up in 4K). “If you could see a 30-year-old negative and what it looks like even when immaculately stored — it was an enormous amount of fixing, just digs and scratches and cinch,” he told EW at the time.

That kind of image restoration technology was around long, long before the Anthropic IPO failed to save the stock market, but its level of precision has increased enormously in the past year. There were also sequences in the stored “Se7en,” though, where generative tech filled in gaps from the original. For one example, Fincher talked about a moment where a camera pan overshot the mark and changedh a shot. The performance had been good enough to use a technically flawed take — and, combined wit an unused take, allowed software to generate the missing information and restore the intended image.

“It ends up being the most thrillingly stupid fix in the world because if you see it, we didn’t do our jobs. And you probably won’t see it. You probably won’t be aware that it’s happened. But you look at it, and you just think to yourself, ‘It’s so nice that we can fix that kind of stuff today,'” Fincher told Collider about that moment in “Se7en.”.

Industry observers note that by Fincher’s own lights, then, the problem with AI in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is that people are painfully aware of it. AI critics might make a distinction between video restoration tools that work on existing projects and those tools being used because they can more swiftly and cheaply generate originals that would’ve otherwise needed to be crafted by human hands. Having something AI-generated isn’t necessarily better than nothing when it comes to art, and choosing to AI-generate a Western chase sequence inside of, say, 10 seconds isn’t a solution to all.

In a recent development, still, Fincher knows what he’s doing. This past week, he emphasized to the LA Times that he’s not a Luddite when it comes to film: “We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old, and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

In a recent development, the answer is an emphatic “No!” to some And they can certainly be mad, or disappointed, or disheartened about Fincher’s decision to use AI tools. The one thing they shouldn’t be is surprised.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that netflix's eight-episode fantasy mystery series is a masterclass in book adaptations. Adapting a book for the small screen is never easy, especially in genres like fantasy and sci-fi. While the TV format gives adaptations room to include more book-accurate details than movie scripts generally do, there's always a risk of alienating readers, changing characters beyond recognition, or shuffling events and compromising the story's timeline.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, though, an adaptation gets it right, staying faithful to the source material while creating an engaging, latest interpretation of a beloved story. This is the case for Netflix's eight-episode adaptation of Lockwood & Co. Based on the books by YA author Jonathan Stroud, Lockwood & Co. is a supernatural fantasy mystery series set in an alternate reality, an '80s-esque version of the UK where ghosts have overrun the world of the living and kids and teens are the only ones with the ability to see, hear, and, as such, fight them.

Trying to make a name for themselves in the UK's competitive paranormal detection industry are independent agents Anthony Lockwood (Cameron Chapman), Lucy Carlyle (Ruby Stokes), and George Karim (Ali Hadji-Heshmati). From their home base in Portland Row, London, Anthony and his friends/co-workers investigate the city's most terrifying hauntings and apparitions, crossing paths with some of the city's most dangerous (and powerful) people in the process.

The show perfectly captures the books' eerie, vintage atmosphere, and it never skimps on the horror, either. Even though Stroud's five-book saga is written for a younger audience, it's still complex and layered; the characters and the overarching conspiracy are developed with real depth. These books are enjoyable whether you're 14 or 40. The show is the same. Most importantly, the chemistry between Anthony, Lucy, and George is impeccable. The cast does a great job of portraying their book characters. Newcomer Chapman is especially impressive as ringleader Anthony, dashing and witty yet vulnerable, too.

For a TV adaptation, Lockwood & Co. remains surprisingly faithful to the books, and not just aesthetically or character-wise. In fact, the show cleverly adapts the first two full-length books in Stroud's series, The Screaming Staircase and The Whispering Skull, into one eight-episode season, without compromising on character development or the story's biggest paranormal mysteries. In an interview with RadioTimes, director Joe Cornish revealed that it only left out one major set piece from the first two books. That's genuinely impressive.

The Dagger in the Desk (standalone novella).

It has been revealed that lockwood & Co.'s biggest book changes are George's name — George Karim, rather than George Cubbins, to better reflect Hadji-Heshmati's British-Iranian heritage — and Lucy's backstory. The adaptation expands and directly depicts Lucy's trauma of working as an agent in the countryside before making her way to London, including her friend and fellow agent Norrie becoming "ghost locked," a kind of paralytic coma caused by certain types of powerful ghosts. This only helps strengthen her resolve and, eventually, her relationships with Anthony and George.

In a recent development, tragically, like so many other supernatural dramas on Netflix, Lockwood & Co. was canceled after its first season. It's a genuine shame, though. Not only was it one of Netflix's best book adaptations, but it would have realistically only needed two more seasons to tell the saga's full story. They could have finished it before Netflix's three-season cutoff — as Deadline reported, Netflix's pay bumps and bonuses tend to jump after a third season, which makes originals more expensive to produce — and filled the gap between seasons of similar highlights like Stranger Things and Wednesday.

Even so, the show is still certainly worth a look. Critics and audiences agree: it has a rare 100% Rotten Tomatoes critics' score and an extremely impressive 94% audience score. Since the last Lockwood & Co. book was published in 2017, the story is complete. Those interested in what's behind Lockwood's mysterious private door, the identity of the ghost in the jar, or the origin of The Problem will certainly enjoy (re)reading Stroud's book series after watching the show — even from the beginning.

Sources indicate that all episodes of Lockwood & Co. are streaming on Netflix.

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1147 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space.
  • According to recent reports, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most vital tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

According to recent reports, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Industry observers note that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

It has been revealed that game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

Sources indicate that first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

Sources indicate that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

It has been revealed that the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for upcoming hardware, this might be your best bet.

Industry observers note that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (745 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

Anya Taylor-Joy’s Sci-Fi Thriller Is Still Her Greatest Movie 2 Years Later

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anya Taylor-Joy has brought so much to her many hits over the years, but her greatest movie is the one where she says the least.
  • Recent findings suggest that set years before the events of Fury Road, in the radioactive wasteland of post-apocalyptic Australia, the film follows the path of Furiosa from childhood, where she is played by Alyla Browne, to early adulthood, where Taylor-Joy takes over.
  • The movie is the fifth in the Mad Max franchise, but the first not to prominently feature the character of Max Rockatansky (who appears in a cameo played by Jacob Tomuri, Tom Hardy’s stunt double in Fury Road) — though many fans of the 2015 movie argue that Theron’s performance as Furiosa was the most compelling in the film, and that she was the story’s true lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anya Taylor-Joy has brought so much to her many hits over the years, but her greatest movie is the one where she says the least. The 2024 prequel Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga sees her take over the title role from Charlize Theron and portray the early years of the post-apocalyptic warrior who became the highlight of 2015’s Mad Max: Fury Road. With George Miller’s direction and Taylor-Joy’s exceptional on-screen presence, the movie became an instant classic.

Recent findings suggest that set years before the events of Fury Road, in the radioactive wasteland of post-apocalyptic Australia, the film follows the path of Furiosa from childhood, where she is played by Alyla Browne, to early adulthood, where Taylor-Joy takes over. Stolen from her idyllic sanctuary home and forcibly adopted by warlord Dementus (Chris Hemsworth), she rises up the ranks of the Citadel, ruled by the tyrannical Immortan Joe (Lachy Hulme). She becomes caught in the middle of the rivalry between the two men, and begins using their ambition to exact revenge and work her way to freedom.

The movie is the fifth in the Mad Max franchise, but the first not to prominently feature the character of Max Rockatansky (who appears in a cameo played by Jacob Tomuri, Tom Hardy’s stunt double in Fury Road) — though many fans of the 2015 movie argue that Theron’s performance as Furiosa was the most compelling in the film, and that she was the story’s true lead. This prequel fulfills that potential with a captivating adventure worthy of its lofty predecessors.

Narratively speaking, Furiosa is an expansion of the world that was introduced in Fury Road. The 2015 film demonstrated us the landscape passing by at 100 miles per hour, in what was essentially one big, beautiful chase movie. Max’s mission was simple – race to escape the Citadel, and then turn back to reclaim it. Furiosa’s origin story is more complex, divided into chapters and focused more on the characters involved. The torment she endures, and the loss that hardens her, are all essential to the plot, making for a much darker and more thoughtful movie.

Industry observers note that both are classics, but Miller’s approach is different each time. Fury Road is a practically perfect example of an action movie, with choreography and spectacle that has few equals before or since. Furiosa is an epic revenge tragedy, examining the harrowing path one must take to be compelled to overthrow tyranny. Furiosa must endure, waiting for a moment that is far in the distance, while clinging to the things that keep her soul alive. We also see more world-building, as it is revealed how the Citadel, Gas Town, and Bullet Farm interact. It is an immersive experience, different from Fury Road but brilliant in its own way.

Sources indicate that furiosa is a character who has learned to fly under the radar, blend into any setting, and survive at all costs. This means a character who is very careful with her words, resulting in a leading role with around 30 lines of dialogue. You might think this would be a hindrance for a star, but Taylor-Joy makes it a strength. Using everything except words, she conveys a character being molded into her environment, learning to be relentless and endure anything in the name of getting home. That means a performance that is conveyed by expression, movement, and the smallest of gestures. Great actors overcome limitations to tell stories, and the Golden Globe winner rose to the challenge.

Looking back on the film, the actor said that Miller had a very specific idea of how she should hold her face, meaning she could only use her eyes to convey emotions for large portions of the movie. “As an actor, where your job is to be able to telegraph how you’re feeling with absolutely everything at your disposal," she told GQ. "To suddenly have everything gone other than [your eyes] was quite petrifying.”.

Industry observers note that the gamble paid off, however, as she delivered a soulful, determined performance in the middle of a large-scale action thriller. There are few actors with the discipline, presence, and talent to not only take up the mantle of a beloved character, but to make it their own, and that’s exactly what Taylor-Joy does. For all the many hits of her past, and the exciting projects to come, Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga has a special place in her filmography.

Microsoft made an official announcement for the Wave 2 updates to Xbox Game Pass in November via a post on Xbox Wire, and while the post mostly highlights the upcoming additions that will arrive during the second half of the month, it also reveals which games will be removed from the service. In total, Xbox Game Pass is losing eight games on November 30. The blow is huge, mainly due to the fact that all games are removed simultaneously, whereas additions happen spread out during the month. Nevertheless, there’s still time to play some of them if you want.

Most of the eight games that are being removed from the service on November 30 have been available in the catalog for some time. For example, the benefit of having Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden on Game Pass is coming to an end over a year after the title’s addition to the library. There are several other games that have been available for free via the service for even longer. This is the last opportunity to play them without having to pay anything extra, but there is good news for players interested in any of the titles leaving the service.

All these games can be played for free until they are removed from the catalog, but if you want to finish a campaign you started or perhaps didn’t have time to even start one of them, know that these games are all on sale for a limited time. In case none of these games speak to you, you can instead look for some of the November additions to Xbox Game Pass, as there have been tons of them over the past few weeks.

Sources indicate that if that doesn’t do it for you, an alternative is to blueprint ahead for some of the first December games on Xbox Game Pass, both of which are co-op experiences. Microsoft will certainly announce more titles to join the catalog throughout the next month, but the first two ones have already been announced during the Wave 2 updates for November.

November 30 may not be as grim as November 15 was for the subscription service, but the removal of eight games at once will hit it hard. Even so, it seems like Xbox Game Pass has a bright horizon ahead of it, so be sure to check out the catalog for any recent updates and look forward to the new free releases.

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a substantial discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is presently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

It has been revealed that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink swiftly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Recent findings suggest that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 rolled out at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing fresh firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In a recent development, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Latest Update: Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps.
  • Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable people to generate nonconsensual nude images.
  • According to the updated rules, apps that allow owners to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable people to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow owners to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow customers to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed consumers to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of Upcoming Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same complications.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

According to recent reports, keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, noted that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

It has been revealed that update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple noted:.

“We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for consumers. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The manufacturer added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

In a recent development, just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

Recent findings suggest that as for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company stated that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

According to recent reports, apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps notable challenges and leaves out key context. The organization says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

Industry observers note that there are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The company defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also indicates it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

Industry observers note that as for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out fresh child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

6 Intense War Films of the 2010s, Ranked by Rotten Tomatoes Score

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Brewster is a filmmaker, critic, screenwriter, and actor whose work sits at the intersection of film culture, craft analysis, and storytelling.
  • He is a movie list contributing writer at Collider and a contributing writer for High on Films, where he covers contemporary cinema, independent film, and festival releases with an eye toward narrative structure, performance, and visual language.
  • In a recent development, ben is an active film festival participant, having worked with Newport Film, the Nantucket Film Festival and as a screener for the Austin, Boston & Woodstock film festivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Brewster is a filmmaker, critic, screenwriter, and actor whose work sits at the intersection of film culture, craft analysis, and storytelling.

He is a movie list contributing writer at Collider and a contributing writer for High on Films, where he covers contemporary cinema, independent film, and festival releases with an eye toward narrative structure, performance, and visual language.

In a recent development, ben is an active film festival participant, having worked with Newport Film, the Nantucket Film Festival and as a screener for the Austin, Boston & Woodstock film festivals. He brings to that work a programming instinct shaped by years of close engagement with independent and documentary cinema. This comes with a deep investment in the kinds of films that rarely find their way into the mainstream conversation without someone willing to advocate for them.

Recent findings suggest that his background spans documentary and narrative filmmaking, film marketing, and production, including work with award-winning directors. This as well as developing his own indie production organization, Lilac Creative Studio, through which he develops and produces original work across fiction and nonfiction forms. His debut documentary, Diamond in the Rust, is an examination of economic redevelopment and displacement in the Queens area of New York City. The film was recently accepted to the Unisphere Film Festival, the Defense of Democracy Film Festival, and the Urbanite Arts & Film Festival. This would mark his first festival recognition as a director. In addition to his writing and programming work, Ben hosts Beneath the Bloom, a film podcast exploring the work behind the scenes in cinema, and the struggles one can face to make a movie become a reality. The show reflects the same sensibility that runs through all of his work. A conviction that film is not merely entertainment but one of the most powerful tools human beings have for understanding each other.

Across mediums, his work is driven by a deep belief in film as a communal, transformative art form.

In the 2010s, war films felt odd and hard to pin down. The fighting in Iraq and Afghanistan was still running its course. At the same time, World War II veterans were passing away one by one. Hollywood looked two ways in response. It nodded back to the older "good war" stories that shaped the genre for years. It also faced newer conflicts that did not end neatly. No clear heroes always demonstrated up. Because of that, many movies seemed to argue with each other about what a war film is supposed to do and what it is supposed to stand for in this decade.

It has been revealed that the top films from that era share one main trait: intensity. This was the period of films that try to place you right in the middle of events. Directors like Christopher Nolan and Sam Mendes leaned into major, crisp images and shots that do not cut away for a long time. The goal was simple, even if the work was not. Put the viewer in the mud and the water. Other filmmakers, including Kathryn Bigelow and Peter Berg, leaned toward a documentary kind of drive. Their stories often felt like they came straight from headlines. Even the sound mattered a lot. In several cases, major awards recognized the way these films made gunshots, machinery and quiet hit hard in the gut.

According to recent reports, some movies in this list got mixed reviews from critics. A few of the highest earners also stirred strong reactions. This happened most often when the films dealt with tense recent history. If you sort them by Rotten Tomatoes scores, you get a quick, not necessarily wholistic view of what some critics thought at the time. That method is by no means perfect. Scores do not always say how a film has held up later. They also do not always match what viewers liked. The range here is wide. There are grim POW survival stories. There are also very detailed retellings of real military missions, scene by scene. These are the most intense war films of the decade, ranked.

Angelina Jolie directed Unbroken, based on Laura Hillenbrand's 2010 book about Olympic runner and bombardier Louis Zamperini. The film stars Jack O'Connell as Zamperini, who survives a plane crash in the Pacific. He drifts on a raft for 47 days before being captured and taken away by the Japanese. O'Connell plays him with a wiry, stubborn energy, with Jolie cutting between flashbacks to his boyhood and his running days in between the horrors. He lands in prison camps under the cruel corporal Watanabe (Miyavi), known as the Bird, who runs the prison camp. The great Roger Deakins captured the open ocean and shot the muddy camps in wide, painterly-like frames.

Joel and Ethan Coen, Richard LaGravenese, and William Nicholson share the screenplay credit. Unbroken opened on Christmas Day 2014 and grossed $163 million worldwide. Rotten Tomatoes lists Unbroken at 52%, and its consensus calls it well-intentioned but too dependent on overly familiar prestige war genre beats. Deakins earned an Oscar nomination for his cinematography, and the National Board of Review named the film one of its top ten of the year, despite the Oscar bait it had written all over it. Many felt the story became a long parade of suffering, although the audience score was friendly, landing at 70%. Zamperini died in July 2014, a few months before it opened, and a faith-based sequel, Unbroken: Path to Redemption, followed in 2018.

Industry observers note that clint Eastwood directed American Sniper at age 84. It is a biopic of Navy SEAL Chris Kyle, the most lethal sniper in U.S. military history. He's a Texas cowboy who netted the nickname Legend for his pinpoint accuracy in Iraq. Bradley Cooper bulked up for the role, and plays Kyle across four tours in Iraq, as he struggles to connect with his wife at home, Taya (Siena Miller). Jason Hall adapted the script directly from Kyle's memoir, with the film cutting from Iraqi rooftops to quiet kitchen scenes in Texas. Rotten Tomatoes lists it at 71% from critics and 84% from audiences, and moviegoers gave it an A+ CinemaScore.

The opening scene, in which Kyle must decide whether to fire at a child carrying a grenade, sets a tense tone. A rival sniper known as Mustafa gives the story a cat and mouse thread. Cooper earned a Best Actor nomination, one of six Oscar nominations that included Best Picture and a win for Sound Editing. American Sniper grossed $547.6 million worldwide on a $58 million budget, marking it as Eastwood's highest grossing film, and the biggest January release ever up to that point. Controversy followed, with critics arguing about its heroic portrait of Kyle and its historical liberties. More than a decade later, it landed in Netflix's top 10 with 4.4 million views in a single week.

David Ayer wrote and directed Fury, which follows a five-man Sherman tank crew pushing through Germany in April 1945. It's when the war's last days are its most brutal, and Brad Pitt plays Wardaddy, a battle-scarred sergeant who has kept his crew alive since North Africa. Logan Lerman is Norman Ellison, a young typist forced into the crew, with Shia LaBeouf, Michael Peña, and Jon Bernthal as the veterans who both mock and protect him. Ayer allegedly put the cast through a brutal boot camp before filming.

Fury grossed $211.8 million and opened at No.1 at the box office on a budget of about $68 million. The production used a real Tiger tank, Tiger 131, the only operational Tiger in the world. Rotten Tomatoes lists it at 75% from critics, and 84% from audiences. The consensus calls it a well acted, raw depiction of war that does not fully live up to its lofty ambitions. James Berardinelli praised how it shows the horrors of war without reveling in cruelty, while LA Weekly's Amy Nicholson felt that Ayer wallowed in ugliness. Ayer drew on the real 2nd Armored Division, nicknamed Hell on Wheels.

1917 follows two young British soldiers on a single day in April 1917, and Sam Mendes built it to look like one unbroken shot. George MacKay and Dean-Charles Chapman play Lance Corporals Schofield and Blake, two young British soldiers sent across no man's land to deliver a message that could save 1,600 men from a German trap. Mendes co-wrote the story with Krysty Wilson-Cairns, drawing on tales his grandfather Alfred Mendes told him about WWI.

Roger Deakins shot through trenches, craters, and rivers, and captured a burning town without a visible cut. Colin Firth, Benedict Cumberbatch, Mark Strong, and Andrew Scott appear in brief but memorable roles. Rotten Tomatoes lists 1917 at 88% from 472 reviews, and its consensus calls it hard-hitting, immersive and an impressive technical achievement. The movie won three Oscars, garnering a Best Picture nomination as well. It also took home the BAFTA for Best Film and the Golden Globes for Best Motion Picture, Drama and Best Director. The night sequence in a burning town lit by flares and the final run across the battlefield are the most visually stunning sequences.

Zero Dark Thirty opens with darkness and the sound of real 9/11 calls. Kathryn Bigelow directed the film off a script from Mark Boal, her collaborator on The Hurt Locker. Bigelow constantly stresses the stakes, with Jessica Chastain as the lead Maya, a CIA analyst whose obsession has driven a decade's worth of work hunting Osama bin Laden. The film then pivots to harsh and brutal interrogation scenes, with Jason Clarke playing the interrogator Dan, and Jennifer Ehle, Kyle Chandler, Mark Strong, and Joel Edgerton rounding out the cast.

Rotten Tomatoes lists it at 91% from 304 reviews, with an 80% audience score. Boal's script moves like a procedural, with offices, briefings, and dead ends. Critics called it gripping, suspenseful, and brilliantly crafted. Chastain earned an Oscar nomination for Best Actress, and the movie tied with Skyfall for Best Sound Editing. The final 30 minutes recreate the May 2011 raid on the Abbottabad compound in dim green night vision, and the sequence is considered among the most tense in modern war movies. Controversy surrounding its torture scenes has never faded, and some critics now see the movie differently after the 2014 torture report.

Industry observers note that dunkirk divides its story into three timelines, one week on the beach, one day at sea, and one hour in the air. Christopher Nolan depicts the 1940 evacuation of Allied troops through the perspective of Tommy (Fionn Whitehead), a young solider hunting for any way off the sand, and Harrier (Tom Hardy), a spitfire pilot with a failing fuel gauge. Mark Rylance is a man named Mr. Dawson, a civilian who sails his boat across the channel to help rescue troops. Kenneth Branagh, Cillian Murphy, Harry Styles, Barry Keoghan and Jack Lowden appear in the ensemble. Hoyte van Hoytema shot it in large format, and Hans Zimmer's score keeps a ticking clock running in the background.

Recent findings suggest that rotten Tomatoes lists Dunkirk at 92%, with an 81% audience score. Nolan used real ships and planes which gave the beaches and skies a physical weight. The consensus describes the project as an emotionally satisfying spectacle from a writer-director in full command of his craft. Dunkirk grossed more than $500 million worldwide and saw eight Oscar nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director. Between the grand practical effects, the dialogue is sparse, and the sound design carries much of the tension. Critics have called it one of the most immersive war movies ever and one of the best movies of the 2010s.

Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let people edit a Story after publishing.

This means customers will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that customers will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”.

Today’s revision is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting consumers manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

Recent findings suggest that all 26 episodes of Netflix's sci-fi masterpiece series deliver a mind-bending mystery, extraordinary storytelling, and a deeply satisfying conclusion. Following its 2017 premiere, this Netflix series evolved to become a sophisticated, multi-layered time travel series that blends multiple genres ranging from sci-fi and thriller to psychological drama and mystery. Along with all-time Netflix greats like Ozark, Narcos, and Mindhunter, this phenomenal series exists in a class of its own and at the top of its class not only on Netflix, but in all of modern TV.

Dark is one of the most masterful sci-fi series that Netflix has ever produced, with 26 episodes across 3 great seasons that deliver peak entertainment from start to finish. The series ranks in the Top 100 indicates of all time on IMDb and earned a near-perfect Rotten Tomatoes score of 95%, along with an RT audience score of 94%, which cements its modern masterpiece status. If you're looking for your next elite Netflix series to binge right now, Dark is considered must-see television and is worth checking out for fans of psychological sci-fi thrillers.

Recent findings suggest that one of the reasons why Dark is considered a modern masterpiece on Netflix is its complex overlap between four interconnected families. What begins as a seemingly straightforward missing persons case evolves into an intricate time-travel mystery that rewards even the most minute details across its three seasons. The series also jumps between timelines, beginning with three distinct eras in 1953, 1986, and 2019​​​​​​. While the scope sounds ambitious from the premise alone, Dark successfully pulls it off through meticulous planning, as the series creators originally plotted out a tight 3-season arc from the very beginning.

Similar to Paramount's hit survival thriller series Yellowjackets, Dark portrays some of the same key characters at different ages between its various timelines. The fun of watching the series is discovering how seemingly unrelated events form a vast interconnected web, giving viewers the opportunity to actively engage in the unfolding narrative with an investigative lens. The time travel aspect is also far from being a plot gimmick, enriching the series through an innovative structure that reveals deeper sentiments about character, morality, and fate.

Dark also rests on the metaphysical concept of predestination, diving into fascinating inquiries about whether any one person is truly in charge of their individual destiny, and whether the notion of going back in time to achieve a more desirable present outcome is attainable or for a greater good. Inevitability then comes into play, which encourages viewers to explore their own ideas on the subjects. It's this type of intricate detail with larger-than-life magnitude that separates Dark from all other Netflix sci-fi series.

It has been revealed that rather than leaving audiences empty-handed with unresolved conclusions, plot holes, and unfulfilled character arcs, Dark delivers in its final season with one of modern sci-fi's most satisfying endings. Without giving anything away, the third season expands the scope of the original time travel phenomenon and actually makes the story clearer when it could have very easily become convoluted. Dark truly comes around full circle by its ending, drawing back to occurrences from its earliest episodes, which even makes it worth watching a second time.

Industry observers note that critics were nearly unanimous in their praise for Dark season 3, with The Daily Beast summarizing the viewing experience best. "Watching Dark's third and final season is like clutching the hand of a person who's dangling from a helicopter over a vast canyon—you're just holding on for dear life, desperate to maintain your grip on the wild situation." Similarly, RogerEbert.com writes, "One of the most mind-melting shows on television, and possibly the most unique Netflix original, Dark finishes its run with peak writing, shocking conclusions, and a bittersweet sense of finality.".

You are a Dutton — or you might as well be. You don't need a throne. You build one, wherever you happen to land.

It has been revealed that you carry the weight of a system that is broken by design, and you do it anyway — because someone has to, and because you're the only one positioned to do it without the whole thing collapsing. Mike McLusky's world is for people who are comfortable operating where there are no good options, only less catastrophic ones. You speak every language: law enforcement, criminal, political, human. That fluency makes you invaluable and it makes you a target. You've made your peace with both. Mayor of Kingstown belongs to people who understand that keeping the peace is not the same as being at peace — and who do the job regardless.

Sources indicate that but just like the Duttons, the Jackson family has problems of its own. Between an alcoholic son and a granddaughter whose resentment toward the ranch is driving a wedge between her and her father, Beulah is struggling to keep the 10-Petal legacy intact. And just when the Duttons begin settling into their newly introduced home, hoping to give Carter a safer future and finally find some much-needed peace themselves, things take a turn when Rip discovers a corpse on their property in the middle of the night.

Industry observers note that like everyone in Yellowstone, Beth and Rip are notoriously prone to aggression, whether they're dishing it out or on the receiving end. Beth has learned to mask her trauma by making herself untouchable. Anyone who messes with her, be it Jamie (Wes Bentley), Summer (Piper Perabo), or a random woman hitting on her husband at a bar, is bound to get a beating. The same goes for Rip. As the de facto enforcer of the Dutton Ranch, it's his job to protect the property at all costs. That means unleashing a raging bull into a bar or confronting a motorcycle gang with nothing but a branding iron.

Sources indicate that things are different in Dutton Ranch. Beth and Rip now have Carter to look after, and the kind of life they led in Montana could put their son's future at risk. Beth is particularly aware of this, refusing to let Carter follow in their footsteps as a rancher and pushing him to finish school instead. Although they're still knee-deep in the ranching business, their priorities have shifted. Rather than getting caught up in blind ambition that defined Yellowstone, Beth and Rip are more concerned with keeping their family afloat and building a home where Carter can have a better future. Local competition still threatens their livelihood, but they're no longer looking to seize everything in sight.

Unfortunately, trouble never stays away for long in Dutton Ranch. Ironically enough, Beth and Rip aren't even the ones starting it. Expanding their modest ranch while competing against a local cattle dynasty is already hard enough, but no amount of ranching experience can prepare them for the messes that keep landing on their doorstep. A dead body turns up on their property, and their cattle contract foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), forcing them to lose their entire herd overnight.

In a recent development, but the real danger starts when Beth and Rip get caught up in the 10-Petal Ranch drama. They initially step in to help the struggling Jackson family, only to stumble upon a much bigger operation involving cattle smuggling and fentanyl trafficking. That's a whole different level of criminal activity, even by Dutton standards. And if there's one sign that Dutton Ranch is heading back toward Yellowstone's bloody roots in Season 2, it's the Season 1 finale. After Beth and Rip expose the operation, cartel associates retaliate by kidnapping Carter. Beth and Rip wanted a fresh start in Texas, but with Carter taken, their turbulent past is catching up with them. Come Season 2, Dutton Ranch looks ready to go down the same bloody path as Yellowstone.

Seeking a fresh start beyond Yellowstone’s past, Beth and Rip confront relentless obstacles and a powerful competing ranch unwilling to yield control.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a fresh interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month.
  • Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.
  • In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue stated Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a fresh interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue stated Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:.

Industry observers note that we were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:.

Industry observers note that when we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a significant way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:.

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are latest or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very notable to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a fresh logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:.

Industry observers note that we could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The glitch of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:.

According to recent reports, well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a tech giant and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney+ has some thematically deep sci-fi demonstrates, with a recent eight-part entry being a masterclass in exploring existential dread. Many of the best TV shows on Disney+ exist within the sci-fi genre, be it the likes of Alien: Earth or Andor. Both shows, Andor especially, took massive science fiction franchises and explored them in more nuanced ways than usual. While Star Wars does have some depth, Andor's exploration of war, rebellion, sexual assault, and many more thematically rich aspects proved it to be not only one of the best Star Wars TV shows, but one of Disney's best projects ever.

Easily, the show is among the best sci-fi series on Disney+, with another franchise taking a page out of Andor's book. That franchise is the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which has had a lengthy catalog of demonstrates released on the streaming service since 2021. The most recent of those was VisionQuest, which, while still working as an exciting, Easter egg-filled Marvel show full of fights, action sequences, and fun characters, emulated Andor by taking a popular franchise and diving deep into what makes it tick.

Recent findings suggest that in this sense, VisionQuest was a masterclass in exploring existential dread. The entire premise of the show centered on Vision, split between being the physical reincarnation of the hero who was rebuilt as a weapon and the loving synthezoid with memories from before Avengers: Infinity War, figuring out who he was, what that meant, and how to feel the emotions he once did. Existential dread often surrounds a lack of clarity on what humanity even is, which the entire quest was about for Vision.

This led to many extended scenes of Vision and his surrounding characters exploring humanity, emotions, and all of the things that make people what they are. More than any other Marvel series, and, indeed, other shows of its genre on Disney+, VisionQuest put effort into exploring the soul of each and every character by making them confront what it meant to be a caring being, human or not. Across eight episodes, VisionQuest's excellent writing delivered a true masterclass.

These deeper themes may lead some to wonder why VisionQuest's post-credit scene was so intent on setting up Avengers: Doomsday, which, while likely to have depth of its own, is a big, event-style MCU movie. However, VisionQuest was actually perfect for this. VisionQuest's focus on lingering dread and finding connection in others seems to be central to Avengers: Doomsday, too. After all, Doom's vendetta seems linked to the parental relationships formed by the Avengers, and how the latter group is now living stolen lives, given that he lost his child.

Sources indicate that A substantial central pillar of VisionQuest was the relationship between Vision and Tommy Maximoff, his reincarnated son. Vision's connection to Tommy was instrumental in the former regaining his human emotions, while Avengers: Doomsday could explore Doom's lack of a child leading to his villainy. Moreover, the Vision family is key to the multiverse, especially with Wanda Maximoff being revived by Doom. Although VisionQuest's story is relatively self-contained, it seems as though it is a great thematic precursor to Avengers: Doomsday.

According to recent reports, when focusing less on VisionQuest's links to wider MCU aspects and looking at it as a conclusion of the WandaVision trilogy, it becomes clear that this is the gold standard of Marvel Television. WandaVision, Agatha All Along, and VisionQuest are all incredibly unique, from the former's sitcom format and the latter's visual representation of AI thought processes to Agatha All Along's gothic Witches' Road setting. This allows each one to shine as its own thing, rather than a mere product of an oversaturated genre.

Industry observers note that moreover, to match the creativity on display, all three demonstrates are excellently written. Each tells its own story with its own unique cast of characters, while still linking together as a trilogy. More than anything else on Disney+, VisionQuest and its prequels shine as a perfect trilogy, with the show in question providing a masterclass in the exploration of existential dread.
